source.text:
You are right it may have read provocative, but was done on purpose. Felt the urge as so many similar comments have been steadily silenced/downvoted last few years that is really super irritating how blind and ignorant can some people be. This is why I wrote - ‘should you not understand it, keep walking’, because honestly I think even some top professionals don’t see it yet or didn’t see it coming. Well surprise, all unfolds exactly as myself personally expects. I’m sure I’m not alone in this weird comfort of clairvoyance.

This one sided view of open source and what people’s sentiment in 2026 towards it helps nobody. It is literal tyranny and so much evident also in the overall tone of conversations in these circles.

And that is important and holds the key to how we even gonna treat such efforts in the future. This cognitive dissonance of what open source is billed as and what actually people catering to it are ready to do (including the name of the common good or not) is just appalling.

Of course my writing was expected to have exactly the effect it did. And was more of a lacmus test. I’ve long stopped trying to get GNU diehards to understand the LLMs as essentially the very enabler of the ‘free as in free beer’ concept.

But free does not imply community but bargain. Not before, not now, and is very important to understand what it means. Hint: free LLM code does not imply community either. And this super simple fact was so much overlooked. 99% of everyone choosing free software does it for the bargain of it, not for the community.

Why the cognitive dissonance? It is perhaps because it all got started by some very weird hippy folk who are also usually very autistic and self-centred to even think about how the great good they are catering/preaching to suddenly is not theirs to govern anymore. I’ve researched the motivation behind open source projects and how they come to be and it is not so often that these are created out of pure altruistic intent.

Nobody says open source is bad or should go, … the only thing so many people express daily (including with stuff ranking top on the agenda) they can find utility in other means to open source, not only manual labour. And these same people, stating it, are immediately then shut down and cancelled by the entitled herders of software who essentially try to bar automation on the writing level even though being its lone warriors on the applied side of it.
